The first rule of fight club is “you do not talk about fight club,” but the first rule of mouse fight club seems to be “publish your results in Nature.” A team of Princeton neuroscientists recently set up a kind of sparring camp for lab mice to find out how watching a fight influenced their behavior. The team split the animals (all males) into three different groups: fighters, spectators, and novices. For the next eight days, each group engaged in a training regimen of sorts. The fighters sparred against a weaker opponent, the spectators watched two other mice fight, and the novices enjoyed a little play session with a mouse-shaped stuffed toy. Read more: “What Darwin Overlooked About Fighting Female Animals”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
